subject: math
cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume
intro: Angles in a figure are often linked by a relationship you can turn into an equation. Two angles are complementary when their measures add to $90^\circ$, and supplementary when they add to $180^\circ$ (a linear pair on a straight line is always supplementary). When two lines cross, the angles directly across from each other are vertical angles and are equal. Adjacent angles that share a side combine to form a larger angle, and the angles around a single point add to $360^\circ$. To solve, name the relationship, write an equation, solve for the unknown, then substitute back to report the angle the problem actually asks for.

items.prompt: Two angles are complementary. One of them measures $34^\circ$. Write and solve an equation to find the measure of the other angle.

steps: Complementary angles have measures that add to $90^\circ$, so write $x + 34 = 90$.

items.prompt: Angles $\angle ABD$ and $\angle DBC$ together form a straight line (a linear pair). If $\angle ABD = 115^\circ$, find $\angle DBC$.

steps: Angles that form a straight line are supplementary, so their measures add to $180^\circ$. Write $x + 115 = 180$.

items.prompt: Two lines intersect. One angle measures $(3x - 5)^\circ$ and the angle directly across from it (its vertical angle) measures $70^\circ$. Find $x$.

steps: Vertical angles are congruent, so their measures are equal. Write $3x - 5 = 70$.
So $x = 25$ (and you can check: $3(25) - 5 = 70$, matching the vertical angle).

items.prompt: Two supplementary angles measure $(2x + 10)^\circ$ and $(3x)^\circ$. Find the value of $x$ and the measure of each angle.

steps: Supplementary angles add to $180^\circ$, so write $(2x + 10) + 3x = 180$.
Substitute back: the first angle is $2(34) + 10 = 78^\circ$ and the second is $3(34) = 102^\circ$.
Check: $78 + 102 = 180$, confirming the angles are supplementary.

items.prompt: Two lines intersect. One of the four angles measures $(4x + 8)^\circ$, and the angle adjacent to it on the straight line measures $(6x - 28)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of the larger angle.

steps: The two adjacent angles form a linear pair, so they are supplementary and add to $180^\circ$. Write $(4x + 8) + (6x - 28) = 180$.

items.prompt: Two angles are complementary. One measures $58^\circ$. Find the measure of the other angle.
items.hint: Complementary angles add to $90^\circ$. Set up $x + 58 = 90$.

items.prompt: Two angles form a linear pair (a straight line). One angle measures $143^\circ$. Find the measure of the other angle.
items.hint: A linear pair is supplementary, so the two angles add to $180^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two lines intersect. One angle measures $(5x)^\circ$ and its vertical angle measures $95^\circ$. Find $x$.
items.hint: Vertical angles are equal, so set the two measures equal to each other.

steps: Vertical angles are congruent, so write $5x = 95$.

items.prompt: Ray $BD$ lies inside right angle $\angle ABC$, splitting it into $\angle ABD = (2x)^\circ$ and $\angle DBC = (x + 15)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of each smaller angle.
items.hint: The two smaller angles together make a right angle, so they add to $90^\circ$.

steps: The two adjacent angles compose a right angle, so write $2x + (x + 15) = 90$.

items.prompt: Three angles meet at a single point and together make a full turn: $(x)^\circ$, $(2x)^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. Find $x$.
items.hint: Angles around a point add to $360^\circ$.

steps: Angles around a point sum to $360^\circ$, so write $x + 2x + 150 = 360$.
